rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Ten ions, ten jobs. **Na⁺** runs the extracellular fluid and the nerve impulse; **K⁺** runs the intracellular side and the resting potential (the Na⁺/K⁺ pump holds 3-out/2-in per ATP). **Ca²⁺** is the structural and signalling ion — hydroxyapatite Ca₁₀(PO₄)₆(OH)₂ in bone, trigger of muscle contraction and blood clotting. **Mg²⁺** is chlorophyll's centre (chlorophyll a, C₅₅H₇₂O₅N₄Mg) and ATP's enzyme activator.…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Iron is present in haemoglobin because Fe2+ binds oxygen reversibly, and magnesium in chlorophyll because Mg2+ enables the ring to absorb light; deficiency of iron causes anaemia and of magnesium chlorosis."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Citrated blood does not clot*** — remove Ca2+ (citrate/oxalate traps it) and clotting stops: the cleanest one-line proof that Ca2+ is factor IV of the clotting cascade.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — One Ion, One Job This topic walks the roster: **Na, K, Mg, Ca, Fe, Cu, Zn, Ni, Co, Cr** — each metal ion with its own address in the body. The exam's centre of gravity is the two flagship complexes (Fe²⁺ in haemoglobin, Mg²⁺ in chlorophyll) plus the electrolyte pair (Na⁺/K⁺) and the structural ion (Ca²⁺).…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 The electrolyte pair: Na⁺ and K⁺ - **Na⁺** — the principal **extracellular** cation: controls fluid balance and osmotic pressure of blood, and carries nerve impulses (rising phase of the action potential). - **K⁺** — the principal **intracellular** cation: sets the resting membrane potential, activates several enzymes.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Roster one-liners: Na out/K in (pump 3:2), Ca bones+clot, Mg chlorophyll, Fe O2, Cu blue blood, Zn carbonic anhydrase, Ni urease, Co B12, Cr glucose. Hb vs chlorophyll: Fe2+/transport vs Mg2+/light. CO 200-250x.

rows.text: **NEB 2024 (verified PYQ): Discuss the biological roles of sodium, potassium, calcium, and magnesium in the human body.** — **Na⁺** is the principal **extracellular** cation: it controls the volume and osmotic pressure of blood and tissue fluid and carries the inward current of a nerve impulse.…  ·  **NEB 2024 (verified PYQ): Why is iron present in haemoglobin and magnesium in chlorophyll? What happens on deficiency?** — Both are **porphyrin-type chelate rings**, and function selects the metal: **Fe²⁺** has d-orbitals that bind O₂ **reversibly** — exactly what an oxygen transporter needs — so iron sits in the haem of haemoglobin;…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: The chlorophyll question wants the formula written (C55H72O5N4Mg), the Mg role (light absorption centre) AND the deficiency word (chlorosis) — all three for full marks.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The metal is chosen by the ring: a porphyrin chelate that needs reversible O2 binding gets Fe2+ (haemoglobin); one that needs light absorption gets Mg2+ (chlorophyll) — coordination chemistry is the job interview.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Na+ principal extracellular cation: fluid balance, osmosis, nerve impulse. K+ principal intracellular cation: resting potential, enzyme activation; gradients held by Na+/K+ pump. Ca2+ hydroxyapatite Ca10(PO4)6(OH)2 ~99% in bones/teeth; muscle contraction, blood clotting, messenger.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Each haemoglobin molecule carries four Fe2+ ions and can transport four O2 molecules; a CO molecule binds each Fe2+ about 200-250 times more strongly than O2 does.

Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Haemoglobin** | Fe²⁺-haem protein; O₂ carrier of blood | 4 Fe²⁺ per molecule → 4 O₂ | | **Carboxyhaemoglobin** | Hb with CO bound to Fe²⁺ instead of O₂ | CO poisoning | | **Hydroxyapatite** | Ca₁₀(PO₄)₆(OH)₂; mineral of bone and teeth | ~99 % of body Ca | | **Haemocyanin** | Cu-containing O₂…  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why iron and magnesium sit at the centres - Both haem and chlorophyll are **chelate rings** (porphyrin-type) that grip a divalent metal. Fe²⁺ gives haemoglobin its reversible O₂ binding; Mg²⁺ gives chlorophyll its light-absorbing electronics. Swap the metals and neither molecule works — the biology is the coordination chemistry.…  ·  ## 5. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Compare haemoglobin and chlorophyll as metal-chelate complexes.  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Fe²⁺, not Fe³⁺, carries oxygen:** only the +2 state binds O₂ reversibly; oxidation to Fe³⁺ (methaemoglobin) destroys the carrying ability until reduced back.  ·  **Ca²⁺ is needed for clotting — removing it prevents clotting:** citrate/oxalate anticoagulants work by tying up Ca²⁺; blood in a citrated tube does not clot.
